title: Serial Frame Detector
statement: Design an FSM that detects the start and stop framing of a simple serial protocol with one start bit (0), eight data bits, and one stop bit (1). The module should assert a frame_valid pulse when a complete valid frame is received. A synchronous reset clears the detector state.
module_signature: module serial_frame_detector(input clk, input rst, input serial_in, output reg frame_valid);
behavior: frame_valid pulses high for one cycle after a correctly framed byte.
A valid frame begins with 0 and ends with 1.
rst synchronously returns the FSM to idle state.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use unclocked shift registers or combinational frame detection.
hint: Track the expected position within the frame using FSM states.
